paper_diagnosis: Disseminated toxoplasmosis in a double umbilical cord blood transplant recipient
disease_label_per_paper: Disseminated toxoplasmosis with CNS lesion and pulmonary involvement after double umbilical cord blood transplant
presentation_summary: 37-year-old Hispanic man with AML, day 60 after double umbilical cord blood transplant, presented with fevers up to 39.5 C, light-headedness, nausea, fatigue, and generalized malaise.
At day 62 he developed frontal headache/pressure, nausea, rash over chest, trunk, and both upper extremities, fatigue, and fever not responding to acetaminophen.
He was febrile at 38.4 C with heart rate 125 bpm and maculopapular rash; labs showed pancytopenia with WBC 1.61, ANC 1.08, hemoglobin 10 g/dL, and platelets 17.

Despite broad-spectrum antimicrobials and negative initial workup, fever rose to 39.4 C and headache worsened; brain MRI showed a 0.7 cm ring-enhancing left inferior frontal cortical lesion with vasogenic edema.
He became hypotensive and tachycardic with respiratory distress and hypoxia, required intubation, and BAL later had Toxoplasma PCR positivity.
CSF, plasma, and BAL PCR confirmed Toxoplasma; he recovered after pyrimethamine, sulfadiazine, leucovorin, clindamycin add-on, and reduced immunosuppression.

outcome.source_text_value: Despite the severity of his disease and the complicated clinical course, the patient does not have any permanent neurological sequelae and is currently in remission

quality_warnings: CSF/plasma/BAL PCR and pre-transplant Toxoplasma IgG are stored as microbiology/confirmatory evidence with use_in_ranking:false.
Pulmonary/liver nodules on CT were not mapped as toxoplasmosis evidence because the paper described prior hepatosplenic candidiasis with residual lesions.
Hypoxia was reported without a numeric oxygen saturation; respiratory failure is encoded by intubation/mechanical ventilation.
